plain_english: May the first section shine, with its divine parents and heart as the family of supreme nectar.
sanskrit_cite:

prathamaḥ kāṇḍaḥ

vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuś ca pañcamukhaguptarucir janakaḥ /
tadubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayam anuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama saṃsphuratāt // [AgMsv_1.1]

plain_english: May that teacher conquer, whose shining rays of knowledge make our hearts blossom everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
yadīyabodhakiraṇair ullasadbhiḥ samantataḥ /
vikāsihṛdayāmbhojā vayaṃ sa jayatād guruḥ // [AgMsv_1.2]

plain_english: He gave me floods of meanings, bright with reflection and streams, that destroy poverty.
sanskrit_cite:
sābhimarśaṣaḍardhārthapañcasrotaḥsamujjvalān /
yaḥ prādān mahyam arthaughān daurgatyadalanavratān // [AgMsv_1.3]

plain_english: May Shambhunatha, pure and skilled toward true devotees, be pleased with me through speech-flowers.
sanskrit_cite:
śrīmatsumatisaṃśuddhaḥ sadbhaktajanadakṣiṇaḥ /
śambhunāthaḥ prasanno me bhūyād vākpuṣpatoṣitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.4]

plain_english: I salute Shricukhala, greater than teachers, by whose purification I stand freed from grasping.
sanskrit_cite:
gurubhyo 'pi garīyāṃsaṃ yuktaṃ śrīcukhalābhidham /
vande yatkṛtasaṃskāraḥ sthito 'smi galitagrahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.5]

plain_english: May glorious great-minded Bhutiraja conquer, bolder than the guru in rescuing devotees.
sanskrit_cite:
tato gurutaraḥ śrīmān bhūtirājo mahāmatiḥ /
jayatād bhaktajanatāsamuddharaṇasāhasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.6]

plain_english: The joyful consciousness compositions arising from Shri Somananda and Utpala conquer, spreading in all directions.
sanskrit_cite:
śrīsomānandasaṃbodhaśrīmadutpalaniḥsṛtāḥ /
jayanti saṃvidāmodasaṃdarbhā dikprasarpiṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.7]

plain_english: The speech of teacher Shriman Lakshmanagupta conquers, teaching recognition that cuts the world cycle.
sanskrit_cite:
taddṛṣṭisaṃsṛticchedipratyabhijñopadeśinaḥ /
śrīmallakṣmaṇaguptasya guror vijayate vacaḥ // [AgMsv_1.8]

plain_english: Even my bee-mind, intoxicated by the wonder of countless new tastes, is satisfied in supreme enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite:
apy asaṃkhyanavāsvādacamatkāraikadurmadā /
yenānuttarasaṃbhogatṛptā me matiṣaṭpadī // [AgMsv_1.9]

plain_english: Having attained unity with that in one's own self, various sound-riches indeed blossom from it.
sanskrit_cite:
tadekamayatām āpya svātmany eva tathā sthitā /
tad asyāḥ pronmiṣanty eva vividhā nādasaṃpadaḥ // [AgMsv_1.10]

plain_english: Requested by good disciples' ears, I explain sentence meaning again and again in Shrimanmalini, here and there.
sanskrit_cite:
sacchiṣyakarṇamandrābhyām arthito 'haṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
vākyārthaṃ vartaye śrīmanmālinyāṃ yat kva cit kva cit // [AgMsv_1.11]

plain_english: By fitness and abandoning the other, scripture and commentary circulate well in this mutual usage of expressed and expressor.
sanskrit_cite:
aucityenetaratyāgād vācyavācakayor mithaḥ /
vartanāvarta etasmin sādhu śāstraṃ ca vārttikam // [AgMsv_1.12]

plain_english: We bow day and night to those Abhinavaguptas, collections of Shiva moon rays, shining beyond all range.
sanskrit_cite:
ye 'harniśaṃ prakāśante sarvasya ca na gocare /
numo 'bhinavaguptāṃs tāñ śivacandrāṃśusaṃcayān // [AgMsv_1.13]

plain_english: The moon rays of knowledge born from Paramesha's face conquer, able to destroy opponents of world bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
jayanti jagadānandavipakṣakṣapaṇakṣamāḥ /
parameśamukhodbhūtajñānacandramarīcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.14]

plain_english: From unrestrained true being, sharing one nature with beings, great knowledge born before has the glory of its rays.
sanskrit_cite:
aniyantritasadbhāvād bhāvābhedaikabhāginaḥ /
yat prāg jātaṃ mahājñānaṃ tadraśmibharavaibhavam // [AgMsv_1.15]

plain_english: Spread and such, it is free from maya's rejectable and acceptable, differentiated only by various thought rays.
sanskrit_cite:
tataṃ tādṛk svamāyīyaheyopādeyavarjitam /
vitatībhāvanācitraraśmitāmātrabheditam // [AgMsv_1.16]

plain_english: That heart of the supreme lord has the nature of reflection; even there Maheshvara always acts by power made of his own self.
sanskrit_cite:
abhimarśasvabhāvaṃ tad dhṛdayaṃ parameśituḥ /
tatrāpi śaktyā satataṃ svātmamayyā maheśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.17]

plain_english: When, having reached contact, he would go to supreme absorption, then his supreme face becomes the seat of emission expansion.
sanskrit_cite:
yadā saṃghaṭṭam āsādya samāpattiṃ parāṃ vrajet /
tadāsya paramaṃ vaktraṃ visargaprasarāspadam // [AgMsv_1.18]

plain_english: The seed of all stands, beautiful world bliss rising from supreme expansion, by non-difference of future face.
sanskrit_cite:
anuttaravikāsodyajjagadānandasundaram /
bhāvivaktrāvibhāgena bījaṃ sarvasya yat sthitam // [AgMsv_1.19]

plain_english: That opinion, heart pulse vision supreme flow wave etc, is the supreme trika before, undivided from all powers.
sanskrit_cite:
hṛtspandadṛkparāsāranirnāmormyādi tan matam /
etat paraṃ trikaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvaśaktyavibhāgavat // [AgMsv_1.20]

plain_english: Here, from release of expansion and contraction doubt, only the three of will, knowledge, and action remain in absorption in own bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
atra bhāvasamullāsaśaṅkāsaṃkocavicyuteḥ /
svānandalīnatāmātramātricchākarmadṛktrayam // [AgMsv_1.21]

plain_english: Thus teachers described it in the Shaiva view: he stands absorbed in experience of consciousness bliss only.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca guravaḥ śaivadṛṣṭāv itthaṃ nyarūpayan /
sa yad āste cidāhlādamātrānubhavatallayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.22]

plain_english: That will, so much knowledge, and so much action indeed occur by harmony of three subtle powers.
sanskrit_cite:
tad icchā tāvatī jñānaṃ tāvat tāvat kriyā hi sā /
susūkṣmaśaktitritayasāmarasyena vartate // [AgMsv_1.23]

plain_english: Supreme in consciousness-form bliss would be undivided from that; but, it is asked, in such a world-self, from abandoning contraction?
sanskrit_cite:
cidrūpāhlādaparamas tadābhinno bhaved iti /
nanu cedṛśi viśvātmabhūte saṃkocavarjanāt // [AgMsv_1.24]

plain_english: How are scripture and other riches said to be rooted in conceptual construction? All this knowledge is made of consciousness radiance.
sanskrit_cite:
vikalpakalpanāmūlāḥ kathaṃ śāstrādisaṃpadaḥ /
ucyate sarva evāyaṃ bodhaḥ saṃvitprabhāmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.25]

plain_english: Because it is of the nature of light, awareness is essentially dense with conscious self-reflection; and that light which shines has reflective awareness as its very nature.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśarūpatāyogāc cidāmarśaghanātmakaḥ /
tatrāmarśasvabhāvo 'yaṃ yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.26]

plain_english: Why should that very light not be the flood of scriptures? What need is there for other displays of reasoning? One who is pierced by the supreme goddess of speech would simply abide in that.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva kiṃ na śāstraughaḥ kim anyair yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
paravāgdevatāviddhas tatrāsau kevalaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.27]

plain_english: But it is not variegated by masses of ordinary, māyic letters. As it is said in the revered Pratyabhijñā, what abides in the self shines forth of itself.
sanskrit_cite:
na tu laukikamāyīyavarṇapuñjavicitritaḥ /
uktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñāyām ātmasaṃsthasya bhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.28]

plain_english: Reflective awareness of will does indeed proceed and is not absent from that. The wise know reflective awareness to be the very nature of manifestation; otherwise, manifestation would not be what it is.
sanskrit_cite:
asty eva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate /
svabhāvam avabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā // [AgMsv_1.29]

plain_english: Even if light tinged by an object seems similar to jewels and the like, any reflective awareness at all belongs to the domain of the wonder of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśo 'rthoparakto 'pi tulyo ratnādikair iti /
kiṃca yaḥ kaś canāmarśaś ciccamatkāragocaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.30]

plain_english: When reflective awareness has joy, pain, and the like as its objects, it becomes clear through the surging inner grasp that arises within that reflection.
sanskrit_cite:
hlādatāpādiviṣayas tadāsau bhavati sphuṭaḥ /
tadvimarśāntarālambasamucchalanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.31]

plain_english: Afterward it attains full clearness. And so the teacher has said: pleasure and the like are established by one's own awareness and stand firm on that basis.
sanskrit_cite:
paścāt susphuṭatām eti tathā ca gurur ūcivān /
yathā svasaṃvidā siddhaṃ sukhādi vyavatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.32]

plain_english: For at the time of later determination it is not known in that same way by self-awareness; even so, it must necessarily be accepted as established by self-awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
na hi vyavasthāsamaye vedyate tat svasaṃvidā /
tathāvaśyopagantavyaṃ svasaṃvitsādhanād iti // [AgMsv_1.33]

plain_english: So too here: afterward, on the path where knowledge and the other powers rise, the level consisting of universal non-difference comes to be reflectively apprehended.
sanskrit_cite:
evam atrāpi paścād yaj jñānādyullāsavartmani /
sarvābhedamayī bhūmir yāvad āmṛśyatāṃ vrajet // [AgMsv_1.34]

plain_english: Then, because a noble reflective portion fitting that level becomes clear, that very primordial emission attains the status of scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvat taducitodāravimarśāṃśasphuṭatvataḥ /
tādṛk sa eva śāstratvaṃ prāgvisargaḥ prapadyate // [AgMsv_1.35]

plain_english: This indeed would be fitting, for even in the unconditioned supreme meaning of scripture some trace of practice can be discerned.
sanskrit_cite:
etad eva tu yuktaṃ syāt tathā hy anupadhau pare /
śāstrārthe 'pi samācāraleśaḥ ko 'pi vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.36]

plain_english: That trace surely possesses the powers of knowledge and the rest that will arise in the abode of clearness; and from conditioning it becomes expanded into various manifold distinctions.
sanskrit_cite:
sa nūnaṃ sphuṭatādhāmabhāvijñānādiśaktimān /
uparāgāt tatas tattadvaicitryaparibṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.37]

plain_english: Just as a face appears in water, a mirror, a jewel, or a sword as trembling, round, subtle, long, and so on, so its manifestation varies with the medium.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā mukhasya tadvyaktisthāne 'psu mukure maṇau /
khaḍge cañcalasadvṛttasūkṣmadīrghādikā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.38]

plain_english: Thus, in the supreme form, the treasures of knowledge arise, beautiful with the unlimited triad of heart, seed, and self.
sanskrit_cite:
tad itthaṃ parame rūpe prodbhūtā jñānasaṃpadaḥ /
anavacchinnahṛdayabījātmatrayasundarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.39]

plain_english: But when Bhairava, expanded by power, desires to emit the floods of beings as inner waves of his own surging form,
sanskrit_cite:
yadā tūcchaladākārasvataraṅgāntarātmakān /
visisṛkṣati bhāvaughān bhairavaḥ śaktibṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.40]

plain_english: Then those very treasures of cognition, as if taking on a constraint of slight activity and practice born from that limiting condition,
sanskrit_cite:
tadā tā eva vijñānasaṃpadas tadupādhijām /
īṣatkriyāsamācārayantraṇāṃ saṃśritā iva // [AgMsv_1.41]

plain_english: having assumed all around an identity with the flood of those waves, still remain within awareness-Bhairava, who is beautiful with the bliss of the world.
sanskrit_cite:
paritas tattaraṅgaughasātmatāṃ samupāśrite /
tathāpi jagadānandasundare bodhabhairave // [AgMsv_1.42]

plain_english: In that powerful awareness, satisfied with the mere fullness of being, the state of the power-holder is set aside by its own full power alone.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāvanirbharatāmātrasaṃtṛpte śaktiśālini /
pūrṇayā nijaśaktyaiva nyakkṛte śaktimatpade // [AgMsv_1.43]

plain_english: Such a stream of knowledge, whose nature is reflective awareness, unfolds; and in it some delight arises through the teaching of enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite:
tādṛg eva vimarśātmā jñānadhārā vijṛmbhate /
yasyāṃ bhogopadeśena ko 'pi hlādaḥ pravartate // [AgMsv_1.44]

plain_english: For the fortunate, even the multitude of enjoyments, nourished by confidence in the practice of that awareness, becomes a state of supreme liberation.
sanskrit_cite:
yadīyasaṃvidācāracaryāvisrambhabhāvitaḥ /
bhogavrāto 'pi dhanyānāṃ niḥśreyasapadāyate // [AgMsv_1.45]

plain_english: Here it is said that the deity's delight in worship is full of the stirring arousal of its own primordial power, especially arising from among the Mothers.
sanskrit_cite:
yatrocyate svaśaktyādikṣobhasaṃraṃbhanirbharā /
devasya yāgapriyatā viśeṣān mātṛmadhyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.46]

plain_english: By the surge of sovereign power, this deity, whose greatness is cognition and who has obtained the name of the lordly state, has become manifested and unfolded.
sanskrit_cite:
aiśvaryaśaktyudrekeṇa labdheśvarapadābhidhaḥ /
devo vijñānamahimā prodbhūto 'yaṃ prapañcitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.47]

plain_english: Here too, in the joining and separating of infinite portions of beings, countlessness is attained because of the connection with the non-difference of the prior state.
sanskrit_cite:
atrāpy anantabhāvāṃśasaṃyojanaviyojane /
prāgdaśābhedasaṃdhānād asaṃkhyatvam upāśrite // [AgMsv_1.48]

plain_english: Simply by force of that adjunct, devoid of the state of consciousness-knowledge, are spread the various powers of scripture, action, and knowledge.
sanskrit_cite:
tadupādhivaśād eva saṃvijjñānapadojjhitāḥ /
tāyante vividhāḥ śāstrakriyājñānavibhūtayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.49]

plain_english: This main world is discussed as fivefold, yet the truth remains undivided.
sanskrit_cite:
mukhyas tv eṣa prapañco 'yaṃ pañcātmatvena carcitaḥ /
tathā ca vakṣyate tattvam abhinnam api pañcadhā // [AgMsv_1.50]

plain_english: By active lordship, directing what lacks, desire cessation, and self-abiding, such sentence collections establish the point.
sanskrit_cite:
savyāpārādhipatvena taddhīnaprerakatvataḥ /
icchānivṛtteḥ svasthatvād ityādyair vākyasaṃcayaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.51]

plain_english: In this context, differences made by place, time, and art do not arise; granted, we say so.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv etāvati sandarbhe deśakālakalākṛtāḥ /
bhedā na saṃbhavanty eva bāḍham om iti vacmahe // [AgMsv_1.52]

plain_english: Here time principle is not merely a name, and even great time power does not expand.
sanskrit_cite:
na hy atra kālatattvasya nāmamātraṃ vibhāvyate /
vaibhavy api mahākālī śaktir nātra vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.53]

plain_english: Then, in the undivided self-full state, what is this grasp of speech reasoning?
sanskrit_cite:
tarhy abhinne svasaṃpūrṇe tadā paścāt punar yadā /
parataś ceti ko nv eṣa vācoyuktiparigrahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.54]

plain_english: Here we say truth indeed; in reality, in clear self, even in expanded principle creation and time.
sanskrit_cite:
atra brūmaḥ satyam eva vastutas tu sphuṭātmani /
jṛmbhite tattvasarge 'pi kāle 'py unmiṣitātmani // [AgMsv_1.55]

plain_english: For awareness, these prior and later alternatives do not exist, because time becomes a differentiator only as qualifier.
sanskrit_cite:
bodhasya naiva santy etāḥ pūrvāparavikalpanāḥ /
kālo viśeṣaṇatvena yasmād bhavati bhedakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.56]

plain_english: That qualifier is said to become knowability by difference, as a blue lotus.
sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣaṇaṃ ca tat proktaṃ samaśīrṣikayaiva yat /
bhedena vedyatām eti yathā nīlaṃ saroruhaṃ // [AgMsv_1.57]

plain_english: Awareness is never knowable; knowability is appearing-ness by clarity grace.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca bodhasya vedyatvaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
vedyatvaṃ bhāsamānatvaṃ tat prakāśaprasādataḥ // [AgMsv_1.58]

plain_english: Clarity is that awareness; if another awareness stood, surely regress would proceed from clarity rules.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśaḥ sa sa bodhaś ca na ced bodhāntarasthiteḥ /
prakāśaniyamān nūnam anavasthā pravartate // [AgMsv_1.59]

plain_english: Deluded ones who call awareness non-first-appearing and object-appearance-natured are cheated by their own words.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva vimūḍhā ye bodham aprathamānakam /
arthaprathātmakaṃ brūyuḥ svavacovañcitās tu te // [AgMsv_1.60]

plain_english: Therefore time is not fit to differentiate awareness, nor is that time able to become differentiator of the knowable.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt kālo na bodhasya bhedakatvāya kalpate /
nāpi vedyasya kālo 'sau bhedakībhavituṃ kṣamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.61]

plain_english: The universe is not different from awareness; otherwise it would not shine; pervaded by clarity, variegated being shines.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvaṃ hi bodhābhinnaṃ tad atathātve na bhāsate /
prakāśena samāviṣṭaś citraṃ bhāvaḥ prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.62]

plain_english: Thus universe clarity would be eternal for all; when clarity named awareness is present, it attains clarity-ness.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvaprakāśa evaṃ syāt sarvasyaiva sadātanaḥ /
sati prakāśe bodhākhye sa prakāśatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_1.63]

plain_english: Even if an unlit being is clarity-self and known, that unlit being is darkness as refuge here.
sanskrit_cite:
aprakāśo 'pi bhāvaś cet prakāśātmā sa vedyate /
aprakāśas tv asau bhāva ity atra śaraṇaṃ tamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.64]

plain_english: If an unlit being-self is made clarity-self, surely that being would be destroyed from loss of self-clarity.
sanskrit_cite:
yaś cāprakāśo bhāvātmā prakāśātmā sa cet kṛtaḥ /
nūnaṃ sa bhāvo naṣṭaḥ syāt svāprakāśatvavicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.65]

plain_english: Even rule cannot make clarity not of that form; but this being shines when clarity is present.
sanskrit_cite:
nātadrūpaṃ prakāśaṃ ca kartuṃ vidhir api kṣamaḥ /
nanv etāvad idaṃbhāvaḥ prakāśe sati bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.66]

plain_english: Let this be indeed; but thus unlit clarity-ness, of being and in unlit-ness, when made clear and present.
sanskrit_cite:
astv etad eva kiṃtv ittham aprakāśaḥ prakāśatām /
bhāvasya cāprakāśatve prakāśībhāvite sati // [AgMsv_1.67]

plain_english: Thus a separately manifested entity is not the state of things; enough of separate light, for shiva is so.
sanskrit_cite:
naivaṃ prakāśito bhāva iti vastusthitir bhavet /
tad alaṃ vyatiriktena prakāśena śivas tathā // [AgMsv_1.68]

plain_english: Therefore that light is sung as supreme shiva, whose inconceivable glory is swayed by freedom.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt prakāśa evāsau gīto yaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ /
sa evācintyamahimā svātantryoddāmaghūrṇitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.69]

plain_english: So it shines through those natures in unfailing state; here all-knowingness is not suspected everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśate tathā tais taiḥ svabhāvair acyutasthitiḥ /
nātra sarvatra sarvajñabhāvaḥ kaś cana śaṅkyate // [AgMsv_1.70]

plain_english: I, Caitra, know the pot not the cloth; but this one knows that; this one does not know the cloth; I know both pot and cloth.
sanskrit_cite:
ahaṃ caitro ghaṭaṃ vedmi na paṭaṃ, veda taṃ tv ayaṃ. /
nāyaṃ vetti paṭaḥ, so 'haṃ jāne ghaṭapaṭāv iti // [AgMsv_1.71]

plain_english: I will know or not; before, not knowing; not anywhere; gradually I know, simultaneously, devoid of both.
sanskrit_cite:
vediṣyāmi na vā, pūrvam ajānāṃ naiva vā kva cit, /
krameṇa vedmi yugapad dvābhyām ubhayavarjitam. // [AgMsv_1.72]

plain_english: I know all, yet I know nothing; I am not any entity-self; indeed not I; I am all always.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvaṃ vedmi, na kiṃ cic ca jāne. naivāsmi kaś cana /
bhāvātmā, nanu naivāham. ahaṃ sarvaṃ ca sarvadā. // [AgMsv_1.73]

plain_english: All am I alone; what else could all be? Thus one light unfolds.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvam asmy aham evaikaḥ kiṃ sarvam itarad bhavet /
ityādir eka evāyaṃ prakāśaḥ pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.74]

plain_english: If one were nonexistent, light would not then be supreme; how could it be? Alas fool, how is this to be instructed?
sanskrit_cite:
nanv eko yady asaḥ kaś cit, prakāśo na tadā paraḥ /
kathaṃ bhaved. aho mūḍhaḥ kathaṃ vyutpādyatām ayam // [AgMsv_1.75]

plain_english: One light shines in varied form from freedom; in reality it is neither varied nor unvaried, because of the fault of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
ekaḥ prakāśaḥ svātantryāc citrarūpaḥ prakāśate. /
vastutaś ca na citro 'sau, nācitro bhedadūṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.76]

plain_english: If cloth's light arose in pot's light, that would not be pot-light; it would be two lights.
sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭaprakāśe vastrasya prakāśo yadi saṃbhavet /
nāsau ghaṭaprakāśaḥ syād dviprakāśo hy asau bhavet // [AgMsv_1.77]

plain_english: Let that be or not; this is urged by you; light should not be as pot-self, so it stands.
sanskrit_cite:
so 'pi cāstv eva, no nāsti tad idaṃ tvatpracoditam /
ghaṭātmanā prakāśo 'sya mā bhūd ity avatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.78]

plain_english: That is improper, since light's cognition-nature is self-unfolding; if that is the definition, what is this vain word-net pomp?
sanskrit_cite:
tac cāyuktaṃ prakāśasya bodhatvāt svātmajṛmbhaṇam /
lakṣaṇaṃ yadi tat ko 'yaṃ vṛthā vāgjālaḍambaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.79]

plain_english: Limited light is the definition of inert; cognition is distinct from inert, because it is not measured.
sanskrit_cite:
paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam /
jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate // [AgMsv_1.80]

plain_english: Therefore, since the sun's existence is established, what fool would say how this all-earth-bearing ray is?
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād arkasya sadbhāve siddhe kaḥ khalu bāliśaḥ /
brūyāt katham ayaṃ svāṃśuśubhritāśeṣabhūr iti // [AgMsv_1.81]

plain_english: Therefore, since light is established, all its variations are keepers of all enjoyment and conduct.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt siddhe prakāśe 'smin yāḥ prakāśavikalpanāḥ /
sarvās tāḥ sarvasaṃbhuktayoṣiccāritrapālanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.82]

plain_english: If light were unestablished, who am I, what are you, what darkness? Nothing at all, or silence, or how?
sanskrit_cite:
asiddhau ca prakāśasya ko 'haṃ kiṃ tvaṃ tamo 'pi kim /
na kiṃ cid api vā kiṃ syāt tūṣṇīṃ syād api vā katham // [AgMsv_1.83]

plain_english: Therefore time cannot do anything to beings who share bhairava's light-identity.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt prakāśatādātmyalabdhabhairavabhāginām /
bhāvānām api kālo 'yaṃ na kiṃ cit kartum arhati // [AgMsv_1.84]

plain_english: Alas, then how is the sequence of words like 'tad eti' made? Let it be heard; what was said is spoken again after separation.
sanskrit_cite:
hanta tarhi kathaṃkāraṃ tadetyādivacaḥkramaḥ /
śrūyatām uktam apy etat punar nirbhajya bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_1.85]

plain_english: The light that is this very one appears thus and thus; no other's light shines, but that alone shines.
sanskrit_cite:
yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa evāyaṃ pratibhāti tathā tathā /
naiva cānyasya kasyāpi sa tu bhāty eva kevalam // [AgMsv_1.86]

plain_english: That very one is supremely generous and illuminator of all; being free, his will-power is called freedom.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva paramodāraḥ sarvasyaivāvabhāsakaḥ /
svatantra iti tasyecchāśaktiḥ svātantryasaṃjñitā // [AgMsv_1.87]

plain_english: Resting in self through absence of other, that very rest in self is called the god's bliss.
sanskrit_cite:
sa ca svātmani viśrāntas tadanyābhāvayogataḥ /
svātmaviśrāntir evaiṣā devasyānanda ucyate // [AgMsv_1.88]

plain_english: The greatness of his freedom, non-separate from own form, would illuminate confusions of beings in his own light-abode.
sanskrit_cite:
svātantryamahimaivāsya svarūpād apṛthaksthitiḥ /
svaprakāśe nije dhāmni bhāsayed bhāvavibhramān // [AgMsv_1.89]

plain_english: Illumination is called the power of action in scriptures, by which manifold principle-creation is divided.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāsanā ca kriyāśaktir iti śāstreṣu kathyate /
yayā vicitratattvādikalanā pravibhajyate // [AgMsv_1.90]

plain_english: When illumination does not shine, how is anything conceived? That knowing situated within it is remembered as knowledge-power.
sanskrit_cite:
bhāsanānavabhāte ca kathaṃ nāma prakalpate /
tad asyāntaḥsthitaṃ bhānaṃ jñānaśaktir ahaṃ smṛtā // [AgMsv_1.91]

plain_english: This much is the god's form from self alone; that is called opening, then five powers, then the all-pervading.
sanskrit_cite:
etāvad asya devasya yad rūpaṃ svātmamātrataḥ /
sa unmeṣa iti proktaḥ pañcaśaktis tato vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.92]

plain_english: Whether as three powers, one power, or god alone standing, that power then is the goddess determined in essence-scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
triśaktir ekaśaktir vā devo vā kevalaḥ sthitaḥ /
śaktir evātha devī sā sāraśāstre nirūpyate // [AgMsv_1.93]

plain_english: The world-substance will be said from 'said' onward as supreme; that one alone, being, goes to manyness, says the great lord.
sanskrit_cite:
vakṣyate ca jagaddhātuḥ kathitetyāditaḥ param /
saivaikā saty anekatvaṃ gacchatīti maheśinā // [AgMsv_1.94]

plain_english: This one, firmly bliss-rested in self, is described by sisterly word-arrangements by bhairava and others.
sanskrit_cite:
sa cāyaṃ nirbharānandaviśrāntisvātmasusthitaḥ /
sodaryaiḥ śabdasaṃdarbhair bhāṣyate bhairavādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.95]

plain_english: Whether near or far-going, in reality nothing of this is other; what word-collection could there be, or anything else, of the lord?
sanskrit_cite:
savidhaṃ dūragaṃ vāpi yady apy asya na vastutaḥ /
śabdajātaṃ bhavet kiṃ cid anyad apy atha vā prabhoḥ // [AgMsv_1.96]

plain_english: Thus the god illuminates thus and thus; then according to that, all this sequence of construction follows.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca bhāsayaty eva deva eṣa tathā tathā /
tatas tadanusāreṇa sarvo 'yaṃ kalpanākramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.97]

plain_english: Nor is that mere construction in such a state; then what ground? Thus the god's intentionality, or thus of those constructing.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca tat kalpanāmātraṃ tathātve 'py atha kā kṣitiḥ /
tathā saṃkalpatāṃ devo yad vā kalpayatāṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.98]

plain_english: Thus this light-self, beyond the thirty-seven-fold, doing manifold illumination, the lord illuminates time.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ caiṣa prakāśātmā saptatriṃśātmakāt paraḥ /
vaicitryabhāsanāṃ kurvan kālaṃ bhāsayati prabhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.99]

plain_english: This very manifold illumination is declared as time-power; then according to the shining time-power.
sanskrit_cite:
vaicitryabhāsanaiveyaṃ kālaśaktir udāhṛtā /
tato 'vabhāsamānaitatkālaśaktyanurodhataḥ // [AgMsv_1.100]

plain_english: From ours the coloring 'tad eti' and so on proceeds; that is not there; indeed what is not there, whence is that?
sanskrit_cite:
āsmākīnāt tadetyādir uparāgaḥ pravartate /
na cāsau tatra nāsty eva tatra yan nāsti tat kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.101]

plain_english: Let it be elsewhere; that stands under light's control. Indeed thus others are in the net of principles in pure-impure state.
sanskrit_cite:
anyatra tanyatāṃ nāma tat prakāśavaśaṃ sthitam /
nanv evam apare tattvajāle śuddhetarasthitau // [AgMsv_1.102]

plain_english: In the circle of principles, pure Bhairava existence makes no distinction remain.
sanskrit_cite:
śuddhāśuddhapade vāpi vidyādau tattvamaṇḍale /
śuddhabhairavasadbhāvād aviśeṣo bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.103]

plain_english: We dance, alas; the teaching must be explained with effort, since it turns in the heart of the long-lived one.
sanskrit_cite:
narīnṛtyāmahe hanta yatnād vyākhyeyam eva naḥ /
āyuṣmato yad dhṛdaye svayaṃ viparivartate // [AgMsv_1.104]

plain_english: In ultimate speech there is no pure-impure distinction; yet that distinction remains fixed in fools' minds.
sanskrit_cite:
śuddhāśuddhavibhedo hi paramārthakathāsu no /
sa tu tatkṛta evāste mūḍhānāṃ dhiyi niścalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.105]

plain_english: If the pure-otherness difference is unreal, then scripture disputes only the intended apparent distinction.
sanskrit_cite:
nanu śuddhetaratvākhyo yadi bhedo na vāstavaḥ /
vyācikīrṣitam evaitac chāstraṃ vivadate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.106]

plain_english: Impurity of principles is purified by initiation; hence difference-dominant positions are only local.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhatvaṃ hi tattvānāṃ dīkṣayā śodhanaṃ tataḥ /
ityādi bahudhā bhedapradhānātra yataḥ sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.107]

plain_english: In the nondual there is no duality at all; yet difference appears even in the all-pervading.
sanskrit_cite:
ucyate nādvaye 'muṣmin dvaitaṃ nāsty eva sarvathā /
uktaṃ hi bhedavandhye 'pi vibhau bhedāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.108]

plain_english: That is truly called bondage in samsara by maya, knowledge, and related terms; worldly beings are established as such.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva khalu saṃsāre māyāvidyādibhiḥ padaiḥ /
bandha ity ucyate tatra rūḍhāḥ saṃsāriṇo matāḥ // [AgMsv_1.109]

plain_english: Following that thought gives these beings certainty of pure and impure; and this scripture properly teaches bhagavat yoga.
sanskrit_cite:
taccintānusṛter eṣāṃ śuddhāśuddhādiniścayaḥ /
kiṃ ca śāstram idaṃ samyag bhagavadyogadeśakam // [AgMsv_1.110]

plain_english: They call bhagavat yoga nondual and free from pairs; its teaching would be thus if difference still appears.
sanskrit_cite:
bhagavadyogam advaitaṃ nirdvandvaṃ ca pracakṣate /
tasyopadeśa itthaṃ syād yadi yāvadvibhedavat // [AgMsv_1.111]

plain_english: That is imagined and determined by separating; in nondual Bhairava all-pervading, entry and seating are considered.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃbhāvyate tan nirbhajya nirbhajyaiva nirūpyate /
advaite bhairavavibhau yat praveśopaveśayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.112]

plain_english: Habitual position is absent, for those two live by difference alone; therefore doubt of universal nonduality is removed.
sanskrit_cite:
ābhyāsikī sthitir nāsti tau hi bhedaikajīvitau /
ataḥ saṃbhāvyanikhiladvaitaśaṅkāvyapohane // [AgMsv_1.113]

plain_english: All effort unfolds for teachers and children; therefore duality is spread here by doubting and not doubting.
sanskrit_cite:
gurūṇāṃ ca śiśūnāṃ ca yatnaḥ sarvo vijṛmbhate /
ato dvaitam ihāśaṅkyāśaṅkya sarvaṃ pratanyate // [AgMsv_1.114]

plain_english: That is imagined as far as going, not neglected anywhere; if duality is unrefuted, then one being alone remains.
sanskrit_cite:
tad yāvadgati saṃbhāvya na tu kutrāpy udāsyate /
tathā hi yadi nāmṛṣṭaṃ dvaitaṃ tarhy ekam eva sat // [AgMsv_1.115]

plain_english: Consciousness-Brahman is enough; why is the thirty-fiveness of principles determined?
sanskrit_cite:
cidbrahma tad alaṃ tattvasaṃkhyākalpananirṇayaiḥ /
pañcatriṃśatitā kasmāt tattvānāṃ tan nirūpyate // [AgMsv_1.116]

plain_english: Therefore, having grasped duality's difference-nature as far as it goes, one who rejects it becomes fearless.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād dvaitasya bhedātmasthiter yāvadgati graham /
kṛtvā yas tatpratikṣepas tena niḥśaṅkatā bhavet // [AgMsv_1.117]

plain_english: This indeed is teaching pierced in knowledge; as possible, it tears the diamond wings.
sanskrit_cite:
etad eva ca vijñāne nirbhidyaivopadeśanam /
yathāsaṃbhavi yad vajrapakṣāṇāṃ tad vidāraṇam // [AgMsv_1.118]

plain_english: Thus in the glorious hymn by Bhatta Narayana, salutation to you manifests and breaks worldly delusion.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi śrīmatā stotre bhaṭṭanārāyaṇena tat /
namas te bhavasaṃbhrāntabhrāntim udbhāvya bhindate // [AgMsv_1.119]

plain_english: They reveal knowledge-bliss free from pairs, O god; the word free-from-pairs is made manifest as nondual.
sanskrit_cite:
jñānānandaṃ ca nirdvandvaṃ deva vṛtvā vivṛṇvate /
nirdvandvam iti nirdvaitaṃ prakaṭīkriyate padam // [AgMsv_1.120]

plain_english: Delusions are manifested, and the ca here is wonder-bringing; here nondual is spread before.
sanskrit_cite:
udbhāvyante bhramāś ceti cakāro 'trādbhutāvahaḥ /
iha cādvaitam eveti purataḥ prataniṣyate // [AgMsv_1.121]

plain_english: Path-purification and the like — its incongruence in dualism will be stated: not this without non-difference. But surely, what even without difference?
sanskrit_cite:
adhvaśuddhyādikaṃ dvaite 'nupapattīti vakṣyate /
abhedena vinā naitan nanu bhedaṃ vināpi kim // [AgMsv_1.122]

plain_english: True — but in the nondual principle even difference is not unfitting; for this is that supreme nondualism, which is no abandoning-and-grasping of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
satyaṃ kiṃtv advaye tattve bhedo 'pi na na yujyate /
idaṃ hi tat parādvaitaṃ bhedatyāgagrahau na yat // [AgMsv_1.123]

plain_english: But in difference, with world-beings settled each in its own nature — this word non-difference, I think, divides them out of sheer relish.
sanskrit_cite:
bhede tu viśvabhāvānāṃ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ /
abheda iti śabdo 'yaṃ manye bhedayate rasāt // [AgMsv_1.124]

plain_english: Enough of that — the matter at hand is answered: as the Lord indeed manifests the imagining of difference, so too surely does time expand likewise.
sanskrit_cite:
tad alaṃ prakṛtaṃ nirūpyate parameśaḥ kila bhedakalpanām /
prakaṭīkurute yathā tathā nanu kālo 'pi vijṛmbhate tathā // [AgMsv_1.125]

plain_english: Yet even so he never at any time attains separateness in the ultimate sense — for he is all-at-once, of the nature of consciousness. But surely — O essence of densely packed being-awareness — in awareness, that what I do here is strange, or that I know: would not others too, ordinary Mitras and Caitras, do the same? Or how would they not know?
sanskrit_cite:
na tathāpi ca yāti bhinnatāṃ
paramārthena kadācid eva saḥ /
yugapat sa hi saṃvidātmakaḥ

nanv ittham ekaghanabhāvavimarśasār saṃvedane yad aham eṣa karomi citraḥ /
jānāmi vā tad apare 'pi na maitracaitraprāyā vidadhyur athavāpi kathaṃ na vidyuḥ // [AgMsv_1.127]

plain_english: 'Ah! Here, good sirs, is the very dense knot of māyā. This we declare: here there is neither own nor other, one undivided. 'I know' — that is but the manifestation of a pot-particular; manifold variegated forth-arisings shine in the supreme, thus it is told.
sanskrit_cite:
aho māyāgranthir nibiḍatama eṣo 'tra bhavatām idaṃ hi prabrūmaḥ svaparam iha nāsty ekam abhidam /
ahaṃ vedmīty eṣā ghaṭatanuviśeṣaprakaṭatā prathāś citrākārāḥ paramahasi bhāntīti kathitam // [AgMsv_1.128]

plain_english: Therefore in 'I know the pot' there is no difference at all. But surely — 'this pot appears to me' — difference does manifest! Not so — for him this very pot is Śiva, just so.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād ghaṭaṃ vedmy aham ity amutra bhedo na kaścin nanu me ghaṭo 'yam /
bhātīti bhedapratibhānam asti naitan na tasyaiṣa śivas tathāyam // [AgMsv_1.129]

plain_english: Therefore those headed by Dvaipāyana declared in their own scriptural domains that mine-making itself is death — by way of giving refutation.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva dvaipāyanamukhyās teṣu svaśāstradeśeṣu /
mamakāram eva mṛtyuṃ khaṇḍanadāyitvataḥ prāhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.130]

plain_english: Thus, born of the coloring produced by the time-reckoning adjunct, set forth beginning with 'that' — consciousnesses, even in the supreme principle.
sanskrit_cite:
tad evaṃ kālakalanopādhijātoparāgajāḥ /
tadetyādi pratāyante paratattve 'pi saṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_1.131]

plain_english: Therein, from being of full one nature, all is everywhere too — for otherwise, division being inapplicable, fullness would not be full.
sanskrit_cite:
tatra pūrṇaikarūpatvāt sarvaṃ sarvatra cāpi tat /
anyathā khaṇḍanāyogān na pūrṇā pūrṇatā bhavet // [AgMsv_1.132]

plain_english: Thence, in fullness, in the abode of all-enduring Bhairava: this five-natured teaching-meaning is the Śāmbhavas — on the abiding of śakti and atom-soul.
sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ pūrṇatayā sarvaṃsahabhairavadhāmani /
pañcātmako 'yaṃ śāstrārthaḥ śāmbhavaḥ. śaktyaṇusthitim // [AgMsv_1.133]

plain_english: Having established the supreme goddess, this one abides, surpassed in himself; thus, desirous of emitting beings, from the state of the emitter.
sanskrit_cite:
nyakkṛtyaiṣa parāṃ devīṃ svātmany udrecya vartate /
itthaṃ sa visisṛkṣuḥ san bhāvān visraṣṭṛtāpadāt // [AgMsv_1.134]

plain_english: Formerly he resorted to the surging-bliss-dense state; but in the emitter-state this one shares even in emission-absorption.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvam ucchalitānandaghanām abhajata sthitim /
visraṣṭṛtāpade tv eṣa visargāveśabhāg api // [AgMsv_1.135]

plain_english: While about to become empty, he is still filled with the entry of bliss-power's partial emission.
sanskrit_cite:
riktībhaviṣyann ānandaghanayā pūrṇayā citā /
tāvad ānandaśaktyaṃśavisargāveśanirbharaḥ // [AgMsv_1.136]

plain_english: Present and full of his own power-flow, he became and will be power-depleted, as triple-self varied experience.
sanskrit_cite:
vartamānaḥ svaśaktyoghapūrṇaś cābhūd bhaviṣyati /
riktaśaktir iti tryātmacitrasaṃvedanātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.137]

plain_english: Then he, god of gods, would clearly stand in the creator station; what stands in the present portion, past and future?
sanskrit_cite:
tadāsau devadevaḥ syād visraṣṭari pade sphuṭam /
nanu kiṃ vartamānāṃśe saṃsto bhūtabhaviṣyatī // [AgMsv_1.138]

plain_english: What indeed is known by you? Even in independence, can past and future be divided by a present boundary?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nāma bhavatā jñātaṃ te svatantre 'pi ke cana /
vartamānāvadher bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca vibhajyate // [AgMsv_1.139]

plain_english: That which has not rested where cannot be divided; whence and how could a boundary state of the present be toward you?
sanskrit_cite:
yac ca yatra na viśrāntaṃ tad vibhajyeta vai kutaḥ /
kathaṃ cāvadhibhāvaḥ syād vartamānasya te prati // [AgMsv_1.140]

plain_english: How could boundedness of those two be, even toward that? Is the universe a boundary, or does it arise similarly? Not what?
sanskrit_cite:
tayor avadhimattvaṃ vā tat praty api kathaṃ bhavet /
viśvasya viśvam avadhis tadvad vā jāyate na kim // [AgMsv_1.141]

plain_english: Therefore past and future are rooted in present-named consciousness; if one brings rest there only.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca vartamānākhyasaṃvidi /
rūḍham eveti tatraiva yadi viśrāntim āvahet // [AgMsv_1.142]

plain_english: If here only the whole array of conceptual rays is not expanded, for a moment one would stand with restrained own state.
sanskrit_cite:
yadi cātraiva nikhilakalpanāraśmimaṇḍalam /
avisphārya kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭhet saṃniruddhanijasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.143]

plain_english: That obtains a single tasting of own nectar-expansion wonder, carrying supreme bliss-nectar abundance.
sanskrit_cite:
tan nijāmṛtavisphāracamatkāraikacarvaṇām /
labhate paramānandasudhāsandohavāhinīm // [AgMsv_1.144]

plain_english: Thus indeed the moon would be full of sun-ray union; when then it does not again wish to emit sun-rays.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi sūryaraśmyoghapūrṇaḥ syāc candramā yadā /
tadā sūryakarān bhūyo yāvan na visisṛkṣati // [AgMsv_1.145]

plain_english: So long, resting well in enjoyment of its own orb for a moment, it is called a vessel for satisfying portions of inner world-gods.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvat svamaṇḍalābhoge kṣaṇaṃ viśrāntisusthitaḥ /
antaḥsthaviśvadevāṃśatarpaṇāpātram ucyate // [AgMsv_1.146]

plain_english: Thus, in the heart interior, the moon of own awareness is present, shone upon by the cluster of rays of the sun of being-light.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ bhāvaprakāśārkamarīcinicayāñcite /
svabodhacandramahasi vartamāne hṛdantare // [AgMsv_1.147]

plain_english: Rested in the beautiful inner abundant nectar of consciousness, filled with inner own nectar, it is not vomited outside, because.
sanskrit_cite:
viśrānto 'ntaḥsthitodāracitsudhāsārasundare /
antaḥsthasvāmṛtāpūro vamyate na bahir yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.148]

plain_english: From that, only inside, that one, revolving and rising, consists of I-awareness satisfying the inner wheel of gods.
sanskrit_cite:
tata evāntar evāsau ghūrṇamānaḥ samucchalan /
svāntaḥsthadevatācakratarpaṇāhaṃvidātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.149]

plain_english: As long as it is raised, so long the own sense-process arises, while restrained in the ray-sheet by union of prosperity and absence.
sanskrit_cite:
jāyate yāvad uddāmyet tāvat svakaraṇakramaḥ /
niruddhe raśmipaṭale vibhavābhāvayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.150]

plain_english: Past and future are not divided from the present; as long as there is non-division of those two, what is present-ness?
sanskrit_cite:
na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyac ca vartamānād vibhajyate /
avibhāgas tayor yāvat tāvat kā vartamānatā // [AgMsv_1.151]
